reuse.why: Adds a shared exclusion predicate and reuses the existing category queries and getBudgetData, but three of the five actions call only the template half of it.

duplication.why: The three identical category queries (3/6/12-month averages) stay copied, each with an identical `.filter(cat => !hasSavedTemplates(...))` appended, and setZero adds a fourth near-identical query.

placement.why: The predicate sits in budget/actions.ts next to the actions; the type change in db/types is minor.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, one row type and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: The exclusion rule exists as a named function but is applied two different ways (predicate vs SQL WHERE plus template filter), so a future exclusion is easy to miss in the averaging actions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts set3MonthAvg/set6MonthAvg/set12MonthAvg filter hidden categories in SQL and call hasSavedTemplates directly instead of isExcludedFromBulkActions.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden part of isExcludedFromBulkActions is restated as `c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0` in the SQL of the three averaging actions, a reshaped copy of the same rule.

one_place.where: isExcludedFromBulkActions holds the full rule for copyPreviousMonth and setZero, but the 3/6/12-month averages decide hidden in their own SQL and only call hasSavedTemplates, so the hidden rule is decided in two places.
